description: Derived nodes on live data: Tempo's service graph is edges-only, so every node in these panels is one the response never declared. converters/deriveNodes.ts declares them as fields above the panel so field overrides can reach them — which requires the panel-registered transformations API (grafana/grafana#129992). This stack's Grafana does NOT have it yet, so this dashboard is the before half of the before/after: the graphs draw correctly, and every per-node override is inert except hiding, which the panel still re-reads by name. Kept live so it flips on its own the day the API lands. The TestData version of the same proof is ECharts Relations — derived nodes, mounted into this stack from the repo's own provisioning.
title: ECharts Relations — derived nodes on live service-graph data (LGTM)

options.content:
# Derived nodes

A derived node is a node that the panel creates from an edge endpoint. The query does not supply a separate field for that node.

The metric `traces_service_graph_request_total{client, server}` returns one series for each edge. The `client` and `server` labels identify the nodes at both ends.

The panel can draw all endpoint nodes without a node query. However, Grafana field overrides need a node field before the panel renders.

This dashboard compares three cases:

| Panel | Case |
| --- | --- |
| 2 | The graph with no node overrides |
| 3 | The same graph with three node overrides |
| 4 | Node values when the query supplies edge values only |

In this dashboard, the data path does not expose derived node fields to field overrides. The hide override still works because the panel can match the derived node by name.

panels.title: Control — the live service graph, nothing configured
panels.description:
The query returns one ranged series for each edge. The `client` and `server` labels identify the endpoints, so the panel does not need label renames.

Every node is derived because the query returns no node fields. The `prometheus → prometheus` edge is a self-loop.

Tempo uses `user` as a virtual node for requests that have no client span. A virtual node is part of the data, while a derived node describes how the panel creates a mark.

panels.title: The same graph, with three overrides on nodes nothing declared
panels.description:
This panel uses the same query and panel configuration as the control. It adds three overrides for node names that the query does not return as fields:

- `grafana` changes color, size, and display name.
- `user` adds a subtitle and data link.
- `grafana-assistant-app` hides the node and its connected edge.

In this dashboard, only the hide override takes effect. The other overrides need derived node fields before Grafana applies field overrides.

panels.title: Show node values — a derived node has no stat to show
panels.description:
Show node values is on, but the query supplies values for edges only. A derived node has no numeric value to display.

The panel does not use node degree as a value. Node degree is the number of connected edges, not a service measurement.

Edge tooltips still show the request rate from each edge field.
